What this question exposed (generalizable):

The error was 8 out of 109,625 — a ~0.007% miss, which is the signature of a tiny wrong digit in the **external exchange rate**, not a table-reading error. The gold answer uses the exact 1964 official annual-average **USD/GBP = 2.7926** (GBP = USD / 2.7926). I used ~2.7928, producing 109617. The fix: pin foreign-currency conversions to the exact 4-decimal IMF/Fed annual-average rate, never the par value (2.80), and carry full float precision through gmean × value × FX, rounding only at the final step.
